places.name: Tomonoura
places.connection: The primary real-world inspiration for the film's coastal town. Miyazaki stayed here for two months, sketching and developing the story.

places.name: Studio Ghibli
places.connection: The animation studio where 'Ponyo' was created and produced.

places.name: Seto Inland Sea
places.connection: The body of water depicted in the film. The town of Tomonoura is a port on this sea, known for its calm waters and scenic islands.

places.name: Fukuzenji Temple (Taichoro)
places.connection: A temple in Tomonoura famous for its panoramic view of the harbor and islands, which inspired many of the scenic shots in the film.

places.name: Joyato Lighthouse
places.connection: This historic stone lighthouse is an iconic landmark of Tomonoura and a recognizable feature of the film's fictional port.

places.name: Venice Lido
places.connection: The location of the 65th Venice International Film Festival, where 'Ponyo' had its world premiere on August 31, 2008.

places.name: El Capitan Theatre
places.connection: The venue for the film's United States premiere on July 27, 2009, as part of its distribution by Walt Disney Pictures.

places.name: Toho Cinemas Hibiya
places.connection: A flagship theater for Toho, the film's Japanese distributor, which screened the film upon its domestic release on July 19, 2008.

places.name: A House on a Cliff
places.connection: A specific private residence in Tomonoura is locally believed to be the direct model for the design and clifftop location of Sōsuke's house.

places.name: Koganei Park
places.connection: A large park located near Studio Ghibli, often frequented by staff for breaks and inspiration, contributing to the pastoral aesthetic of many Ghibli films.
